name: hundred-session-proof

spawn_spec.prompt:
TASK: Add a test-only, failing-first proof that Ferryx's terminal renderer lifecycle supports the specified 100 simulated live sessions (five workspaces × 20 sessions) with visible sessions pinned and inactive renderer count bounded by the LRU warm limit.
DELIVERABLE: Modify only `ui/src/lib/terminalHostManager.test.ts`. Return RED mutation evidence and GREEN output from `bun run --cwd ui test -- terminalHostManager`, exact assertions, and changed file path.
SCOPE: This is TEST-ONLY work. Do not change production code, TerminalPane, workspace code, Rust/native code, configs, or package manifests. Use the current public manager API only; no `any`, optional method calls, sleeps, or mock assertions that can pass without exercising lifecycle behavior. Reset any altered cache limit and destroy every created frontend instance before test exit to avoid pollution.
REQUIRED TEST: Create five logical workspace groups of 20 live TerminalSession objects (100 total). Register a small explicit visible set across multiple workspaces before creation, create all sessions, and assert: visible renderer instances remain; number of remaining inactive renderer instances is no more than `getWarmCacheLimit()`; all 100 backendSessionId values/session objects remain intact; no backend close/spawn/IPC API is called; the oldest inactive frontend renderers were disposed. Verify reference-count behavior by temporarily registering a second visible mount for one session, releasing one handle, and proving it remains pinned until the final handle releases.
RED PROOF: Because production behavior already exists, first add the test, then temporarily mutate only the exact cache enforcement seam in the working tree so this new test fails for the intended renderer-budget assertion. Capture the failure, restore the mutation, and capture GREEN. Do not commit the mutation or production change.
STOP WHEN: the single test file contains a clear five-by-twenty deterministic lifecycle proof, valid mutation RED/GREEN transcripts are returned, and no test process is alive.
